title: A dungeon crawler I’ve built almost entirely with AI over a few weeks
author: PrettyPinkPansi
selftext:
The loop for The Still Below is simple, go down into the crypts, gather reagents, come back up to brew and sell remedies, then upgrade to go deeper. Made in Godot.



I'm a software engineer by profession. I set out to use AI as much as possible for this project. Code, Music, Story, Models/Animations. Nearly everything is done through prompting AI. Working with AI to flesh out a story and an identity for the way the game looks and heavy emphasis on boss fights has been my favorite part.



Some things I've learned working on this:

**Models/animations**, I tried Astra 6 and Opus 5.5 using blender, both at Max/Ultra. The popular sentiment is Astra is better but for me it wasn't even close. Neither are AAA, but Opus did far better.

**Music**, Suno makes absolute bangers. This is probably the furthest ahead part of AI generation. There's a short sample in the video of my current favorite track.

**Code,** 90% Opus/10% Astra. I've A/B tested both on the same work and mostly prefer Opus's outcome overall. Fable 5.2 is also great, but it chews through plan usage too fast to be worth it.

**Boss design** has taken up 80% of the development time. Zone 1 boss was quick and naive. With Zone 2 I tried for something that makes you go "oh shit, that's cool". I hope it does! I went much deeper on zone 3 and 4 bosses and can't wait to share them.

The demo has both zone 1 and 2 available. It’s free on [itch.io](https://throughreflection.itch.io/the-still-below) to try out. :)

comments.author: AdHom
comments.body: What is it that makes Claude use those phrases like "cut what grows below?". It's so stereotypically Claude and I find it very annoying. "Targets what you face" "throw what you hold" "explore what the map doesn't show" that kind of thing

replies.author: PrettyPinkPansi
replies.body: The video was actually made by Astra, not Claude. But I agreed! The frontier models both have this sensationalist wording. I follow behind Claude and clean up annoying text in game. It wants to over explain everything.

replies.author: AdHom
replies.body: Oh interesting I haven't used Astra quite as much but from the little I have, I generally preferred it's dialogue and writing because it seemed to use those kinds of stock phrases less. Interesting to see it has the same tendencies. I just want to find a clean way to describe this particular kind of "what" phrasing to prompt against it.

comments.author: PrettyPinkPansi
